messages.author: e52b48f39d670ebd
messages.subject: AJAX in Shiny
parts:
First of all, thank you for the amazing work on Shiny.

I am looking to solve the following -

1) User has 5 plots to rate.
2) As user rates 3 out of those, an AJAX request is sent to do some expensive computation and fetch next 5.
3) When user has rated all 5, the page refreshes with the plots fetched in (2).
4) Repeat (1) and (2) at some interval, say every 5 items.

So this is not reactive. I do not want the plots to refresh as soon as the user rates them. 
However as the computation is expensive, so I do not want the user to wait for them at the end of 5 plots (cannot use the submit button solution). 

Can server.R be coded in a webservice way that html can call with some arguments (say getNext5(user, plots_rated, ...) ) and get back JSON for this? Are there better solutions?

Thanks

messages.author: e52b48f39d670ebd
messages.subject: Re: AJAX in Shiny
parts:
The expensive computation is done in R  (online modelling). It could also be fetched from a third part (database for instance). User's ratings of first 3 plots in this case would affect the next 5 items gotten.
Basically it boils down to this. While the user session is in progress, we fetch something in the background using partial data. When we have it, we queue it up to be displayed next. And we start another asynchronous request in the background to use what we have learnt by that time. I am sure this will require some javascript but want to check which components to use, since I am not very experienced with Shiny yet.

messages.subject: Re: AJAX in Shiny
parts:
The problem is that R is single threaded so while the long execution is happening, the entire server is blocked. I was trying to think of a way of using fork or some distributed processing R package to get it to execute asynchronously but I'm afraid I'm not familiar enough with those aspects of R to tell you.

If you could have a completely separate process for the AJAX calls that would probably be the simplest solution.
